name: Store
_comment: BananaOS's Store catalog (rocknixds-store reads it with RNDS_STORE_PLATFORM=banana). Paths are ROCKNIX's, mapped by the Store: /storage/.config/rocknixds/<id> -> /data/store/apps/<id>, the tile folder -> /data/store/tiles. Döda Kvarter and Bank come with the system ("builtin": removing one takes its tile off the menu, installing puts it back), and so does the Store.

apps.name: eReaderDS
apps.summary: A two-page ebook reader: hold the handheld sideways like an open book.
apps.description: Each screen shows one page. Reads EPUB and text books, and comics and manga (.cbz). Bookmarks, highlights, a dictionary, themes and fonts, KOReader sync, and books from Standard Ebooks, Project Gutenberg and other catalogs, or sent from your phone or computer over Wi-Fi. Put books in roms/ebook on the card (the banana share's roms\ebook folder); your books, settings and reading places stay there, also when the app is removed. Made by casualducko for the RG DS Plus; it updates itself too, and the Store follows its releases.

apps.name: GBA DS
apps.summary: Game Boy Advance on both screens: the game on one, its own map on the other.
apps.description: A Game Boy Advance emulator made for dual-screen handhelds, built on mGBA. The game plays on the top screen; for 37 games (Castlevania, Metroid, Zelda, Golden Sun, Advance Wars, Mario Kart and more) the bottom screen shows the game's own map, race HUD or unit intel and keeps it current as you play, the way the DS Castlevanias do. It finds the games in roms/gba on the card by itself (the banana share's roms\gba folder): it lists the ones it has second-screen support for, and show_all = 1 in store/apps/gbads/gba-ds.cfg lists every game (the others play on one screen). HOME or a tap on the bottom screen opens its menu: save states, rewind, cheats, display options, Close GBA DS. From v1.4.10 its battery saves are the Game Boy Advance list's own (saves/gba, .srm), so a game goes on from the same save in GBA DS and in Banana's emulators; its save states and settings stay in store/apps/gbads, also when the app is removed. In its Settings, GBA DS in BananaOS's GBA list starts the supported games from Banana's own Game Boy Advance list in GBA DS; the others then play in RetroArch without Banana's own second screen, so leave it off if you use that (from v1.4.10, removing the app leaves the list starting its games in Banana's own emulator again). Made by kyannon (free software, GPL-3.0); it updates itself too, and the Store follows its releases.

apps.name: Döda Kvarter
apps.summary: A zombie roguelike for both screens, set in a Swedish suburb at night.
apps.description: Survive round after round as in Call of Duty Zombies: earn kronor, buy your way through barricades into new districts, find the power, drink Julmust and Snabbkaffe, try Lådan (beware the Dalahäst) and upgrade at Smedjan. Every town is new and the loot gets better every round. Eight bosses from Swedish folklore. The top screen is the game, the bottom screen your inventory, health, ammo and the map. It comes with BananaOS: removing it takes its tile off the menu (your saves stay in apps/dodakvarter on the card), installing it puts the tile back.

apps.name: Poketool
apps.summary: A Pokémon bank, save editor, legality checker and trading app, built on PKHeX.Core.
apps.description: Formerly Bank & Trade. Reads your game saves (generation 1 to 5), stores Pokémon in boxes of its own, moves them between games, boxes and parties through the bank (they change format only when they move up a generation, as Pal Park and Poké Transfer did), edits Pokémon (or makes new ones), trainers, bags and Pokédexes as PKHeX does, duplicates Pokémon, checks every one with PKHeX's legality analysis, and trades with another handheld over Wi-Fi, in a lobby or a private room. Close the game before you use it. Your bank, settings and save backups stay in apps/bank on the card, also when the app is removed. It came with BananaOS until 0.5.3 (there, removing it takes its tile off the menu and installing puts it back); from 0.5.3 the Store downloads it onto the Apps shelf.

apps.name: Bshare
apps.summary: Files to and from your phone or computer over Wi-Fi, with LocalSend.
apps.description: Sends files between the handheld and phones or computers on the same Wi-Fi that have LocalSend open (the free and open-source app by Tien Do Nam and its contributors, localsend.org). Receive is off until you turn it on: then you accept each transfer, games go straight into their system's folder and everything else into banana/received, or into a location you choose. To send, mark files or folders on the cards and pick a device. Bshare is Banana's own small version of LocalSend's open protocol. It comes with BananaOS: removing it takes its tile off the menu, installing it puts the tile back.

apps.name: PortMaster
apps.summary: Downloads and runs PC and homebrew game ports, on the Ports shelf.
apps.description: Gets ports: PC games and homebrew made to run on handhelds (many free, some needing files from a copy of the game you own), downloaded from portmaster.games and started from the Ports shelf. Its entry and the ports it installs go in roms/ports on the card (the banana share's roms\ports folder), and so does PortMaster itself; it updates itself. Removing it leaves your ports and the runtimes they need (PortMaster/libs), but a port needs PortMaster's folder to start: install it again to play them. Made by the PortMaster team (portmaster.games, MIT licence); it came with BananaOS until 0.5.3.
